title: Stable Allocations, Unstable Payment Paths: The Shapley Value and Voluntary Coalition Formation
abstract: arXiv:2609.20421v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The random-order interpretation of the Shapley value specifies both a terminal allocation and a payment path: when a player enters, she receives her marginal contribution at that moment. We ask whether players would voluntarily follow this path. A player may prefer to wait if her marginal contribution is expected to rise as the coalition grows. This creates a tension in convex games. The Shapley allocation belongs to the core, but, except in additive games, the associated marginal-contribution payment path does not support voluntary entry. We separate these two objects by introducing payment flows that divide the surplus created at each coalition transition. Every efficient allocation can be implemented by a local, budget-balanced voluntary flow when signed payments are available. We select a canonical implementation by minimizing the distance from the Shapley flow, and show that the problem simplifies sharply in symmetric cardinality ga

translated_title: 稳定分配、不稳定支付路径：Shapley值与自愿联盟形成
translated_abstract: Shapley值的随机顺序解释既规定了最终分配，也规定了一条支付路径：当玩家加入时，她获得此时的边际贡献。我们探讨玩家是否会自愿遵循这一路径。如果玩家预期随着联盟扩大其边际贡献将会上升，她可能更愿意等待。这在凸博弈中造成了一种张力：Shapley分配属于核心，但除可加博弈外，与之对应的边际贡献支付路径并不支持自愿加入。我们通过引入“支付流”将这两个概念分离，支付流在每个联盟转移时划分所产生的剩余。当允许带符号支付时，任何有效分配都可以通过局部、预算平衡的自愿支付流来实现。我们通过最小化与Shapley流的距离来选择一个规范的实现方式，并证明该问题在对称基数博弈中会大幅简化。
tldr: 论文揭示Shapley分配虽属于核心而稳定，但其边际贡献支付路径无法激励玩家自愿依次加入联盟，为此提出“支付流”机制，证明任何有效分配都可通过局部、预算平衡的自愿支付流实现，并选取最接近Shapley流的规范实现。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that although the Shapley allocation is core-stable, its marginal-contribution payment path fails to incentivize voluntary sequential entry; it introduces payment flows that implement any efficient allocation via local, budget-balanced voluntary transfers, selecting the canonical flow closest to the Shapley flow.
